FROMLIST: mfd: Add support for the MediaTek MT6358 PMIC This adds support for the MediaTek MT6358 PMIC. This is a multifunction device with the following sub modules: - Regulator - RTC - Codec - Interrupt It is interfaced to the host controller using SPI interface by a proprietary hardware called PMIC wrapper or pwrap. MT6358 MFD is a child device of the pwrap. Signed-off-by: Hsin-Hsiung Wang <hsin-hsiung.wang@mediatek.com> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10928149/) BUG=b:126006378 TEST=build and boot to shell Change-Id: Ia5e463bc048b58c140f87772d4dacbd24eb34c76 Signed-off-by: Claire Chang <tientzu@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1598684 Commit-Ready: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ASoC: mediatek: mt6358: initialize setting when ramping volume Mt6358 ramps up from the smallest volume (i.e. -10dB) to target dB when opening and ramps down from target dB to mute (i.e. -40dB) when closing. If target is equal to -10dB when opening, headset_volume_ramp() simply leaves current setting (which may not be -10dB) unchanged. Execute the loop at least once to initialize the setting to the starting point (i.e. from). Signed-off-by: Tzung-Bi Shih <tzungbi@google.com> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit bdb8fa6b09a801a6cbe3c2487f0228860f9c5aba git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/broonie/sound.git for-next) BUG=b:130204930 TEST=insert 3.5mm headphone 1. sox -b 16 -n -t alsa -r 48000 -c 2 synth sine 440 2. ctrl+c on 1 and wait 10+ seconds 3. amixer -c0 cget name="Headphone Volume", should get -13 4. amixer -c0 cset name="Headphone Volume" 0 5a. sox -b 16 -n -t alsa -r 48000 -c 2 synth sine 440 5b. amixer -c0 cget name="Headphone Volume", should get 0 instead of -13 Change-Id: I14105caef79c86b9d29f20901c78aba02c1123fa Signed-off-by: Tzung-Bi Shih <tzungbi@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1596053 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ASoC: mediatek: mt6358: save output volume for mixer controls Output volume settings from mixer controls would be lost. Imagine that "Headphone Volume" has set to -10dB via amixer: - in mtk_hp_enable() - hp_store_gain() saves the volume setting -10dB from regmap_read() to ana_gain[AUDIO_ANALOG_VOLUME_HPOUTL] - headset_volume_ramp() ramps up from -10dB to -10dB - in mtk_hp_disable() - headset_volume_ramp() ramps down from -10dB to -40dB Next time in mtk_hp_enable(), hp_store_gain() would save -40dB but not -10dB. As a result, headset_volume_ramp() would ramp from -10dB to -40dB (which is mute). Signed-off-by: Tzung-Bi Shih <tzungbi@google.com> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit bbb56537a3279f7221e253afc29e834a3d99662f git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/broonie/sound.git for-next) BUG=b:130204930 TEST=insert 3.5mm headphone 1. amixer -c0 cset name="Headphone Volume" 0 2a. sox -b 16 -n -t alsa -r 48000 -c 2 synth sine 440 2b. amixer -c0 cget name="Headphone Volume", should get 0 3. ctrl+c on 2a and wait 10+ seconds 4. amixer -c0 cget name="Headphone Volume", should get -13 5a. sox -b 16 -n -t alsa -r 48000 -c 2 synth sine 440 5b. amixer -c0 cget name="Headphone Volume", should get 0 Change-Id: I3b9281dd6273cdb2db64649dc38eedd12f01b38b Signed-off-by: Tzung-Bi Shih <tzungbi@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1587711 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ASoC: mediatek: mt6358: save PGA for mixer control mt6358_amic_disable() resets PGA to 0. Save the gain settings from mixer control and restore them when using the microphone. CRAS: dev_io - Skip node and stream gain if APM is used Commit fe49965 has a bug that causes unexpected gain to APM use case when we broke down the capture gain structure to node level and stream level. For client stream that uses APM, we should NOT apply any additional gain between HW captured samples and client stream. This change fixes that and adds unittest to prevent future regression.
